Some things I found annoying were that some stages have sets of sideways facing cards which make it a bit harder for your brain to process the information you are looking at and make you have to play slower. I got this regency story-based solitaire cards game on a bit of a whim while looking for a casual game that I could turn to as and when I just wanted a relaxing game experience. Having just fully completed the game and its achievements, I'm really glad that I took the chance on it!

The game consists of 20 chapters, matching "headlines" in the overarching story of the impoverished heroine Bella trying to rebuild her family's wealth and ballroom, so that she can finally host a triumphant Ball and find true love. Each chapter contains up to 10 solitaire levels with varying layouts and obstacles e.g. "lock" cards that cannot be removed until a "key" card is revealed. The goal for each level is to remove all of the dealt cards through sequences, wildcards, and special tools, before the player's deck of cards runs out. One or more stars are awarded for the successful completion (or near completion) of a level; each level can be immediately retried to try to get a better result. Removing cards earns money, and this is multiplied in relation to the number of cards removed in single sequences.

Chapters also have goals e.g. obtaining (or exceeding) a target number of stars or a specified amount of money. A chapter must be repeated if any of its goals have not been achieved when the chapter's final level is finished. At the successful end of a chapter, the player can purchase items for Bella and her ballroom, each giving an upgrade to the game play (e.g. being able to see the value of a hidden card).

Achievements are awarded for game progression, for completing the game in normal and hard modes, and for various play-related performances (making long sequences, using all of the tools, etc). But, putting aside all of the above descriptions of how the game works, the most important summary is that Regency Solitaire  is sweet, cosy, challenging but forgiving (with unlimited attempts at a level, plus the various tools and upgrades), fun, and accompanied by really nice and appropriate music and artwork. In short, a pleasure to play.
